title: Implement OPA-backed RBAC cache, KMS geo-fallback proxy and audit stitcher
author: Priya Rao
description: Summary: Adds an OPA-backed in-process RBAC decision cache to reduce repeated policy evaluation latency, a KMS geo-fallback proxy to gracefully route key operations to a secondary provider when region pinned providers are unavailable, and an audit-stitcher service that coalesces audit fragments from edge proxies into canonical, signed records. Motivation: We saw customer reports of elevated p99 auth latency and occasional KMS outages causing failed operator flows (Linear ENG-9142). This change reduces policy eval overhead, improves KMS resilience for region-pinned tenants, and makes audit trails more robust for downstream compliance pipelines. Design notes: 1) RBAC cache: an LRU with TTL keyed by (service, resource, action, flattened-claims-hash). Policy decisions are still authoritative from OPA but cache hits short-circuit RPCs; TTL is configurable per-tenant and honors explicit policy TTLs from the policy metadata. 2) KMS geo-fallback proxy: a sidecar/edge proxy that prefers tenant-bound KMS providers but can failover to a configured fallback provider (with explicit tenant consent flag). Failover is rate-limited and recorded in audit events. 3) Audit stitcher: receives audit fragments (signed) from regional proxies, deduplicates, orders by event-time, signs a canonical envelope, and forwards to the audit-ingest pipeline with provenance headers. Compatibility/rollout: defaults are conservative — cache is disabled for tenants with 'policy-cache: disabled' claim and KMS fallback is opt-in via tenant flag. We will roll out in stages: alpha (internal), beta (select tenants), global. Checklist: - [x] RFC and design reviewed by SEC and SRE - [x] OPA integration tests added - [x] KMS fallback simulation harness - [x] End-to-end audit stitcher verification with sample tenants - [x] Added feature flags and per-tenant toggles - [x] Updated docs (console + API) Testing: unit tests for cache correctness and eviction, integration tests against a mocked OPA and dual-KMS setup, chaos test that simulates regional KMS outage and verifies fallback telemetry. Observability: new metrics rbac.cache.hits, rbac.cache.misses, kms.fallback.count, audit.stitcher.latency. Security considerations: fallback only invoked if tenant config allows; all fallback KMS operations are tagged and require justification in the audit envelope. Data residency: audit-stitcher marks provenance and keeps 'origin-region' tag; fallback KMS operations include an explicit residency-consent header so downstream detection can enforce export rules. Migration/rollback plan: feature flags allow immediate disable; cache can be flushed cluster-wide and OPA traffic will revert to baseline. Notes on performance: synthetic load tests show ~12% reduction in policy-decision p99 and 18% reduction in mean end-to-end auth latency for CPU-bound operator flows; cache adds ~3% CPU overhead to the operator-auth service under steady state. Follow-ups: - a follow-up PR will add a policy TTL reconciliation job to surface stale policy TTLs - console UI will surface per-tenant cache metrics - extend audit-stitcher to attach KMS usage proofs for high-sensitivity tenants

review_comments: Evan Liu: Can we document how cache invalidation behaves when policies change? Also request adding a metric for cache.evictions.
Priya Rao: Reply: added policy TTL and a policy-watch invalidation hook; metric rbac.cache.evictions included in metrics_defs.go.
Grace Kim: Security question: ensure KMS fallback cannot be used to exfiltrate region-locked keys. Please add tenant-level consent enforcement and audit justification.
Priya Rao: Reply: fallback requires tenant consent flag; we also add residency-consent header in the audit envelope and log an explicit justification entry. Added unit tests for enforcement.
Omar Alvarez: Perf: what is the CPU/latency trade-off? Can we limit cache size per-tenant?
Priya Rao: Reply: added per-tenant max_entries config and conservative defaults; included benchmark results in the PR description.
Grace Kim: Approve after tests and doc updates.
release_notes: Add optional OPA-backed RBAC caching to reduce policy decision latency; introduce KMS geo-fallback proxy (opt-in per-tenant) to improve resilience during regional KMS outages; add audit-stitcher to canonicalize signed audit fragments for compliance pipelines. Admins can control features via per-tenant flags. See security docs for residency and consent implications.
security_impact: low - introduces fallback surface but gated by tenant consent and audited; cache does not change decision authority.
testing_summary: Unit tests (cache semantics, eviction), integration tests (OPA + dual KMS), chaos test that simulates region KMS outage and verifies fallback path and audit envelope; e2e verified on staging with 3 tenants; CI passed all checks.
perf_impact: ~12% improvement p99 policy decision latency under load; ~3% CPU overhead on operator-auth service; per-tenant cache sizing mitigates noisy neighbors.
